questions.prompt: A team wants to measure resources outside its allowed regions before blocking deployments. Which policy effect reports violations without rejecting requests?

options.explanation: It records noncompliance without acting as Deny.
It can reject noncompliant create/update requests.
It changes supported properties rather than only observing.
It can deploy related configuration and is not purely reporting.

questions.prompt: A Modify policy assignment identifies existing untagged resources, but they remain unchanged after evaluation. Which action applies the supported modification to those existing resources?

options.text: Create a remediation task using an appropriately authorized assignment identity.
options.explanation: Existing-resource correction is performed through remediation.

options.text: Wait for an Audit-only policy to rewrite every resource.
options.explanation: Audit reports; it does not apply modifications.

options.text: Assign Reader to every resource owner.
options.explanation: Read permission does not execute policy modification.

options.text: Delete the resource group to clear noncompliance.
options.explanation: Deleting the workload does not implement the requested correction.

questions.prompt: A DeployIfNotExists policy deployed diagnostic settings. The policy assignment is later removed. What happens to the settings solely because of assignment removal?

options.text: They are not automatically rolled back.
options.explanation: Policy removal does not undo its earlier deployments.

options.text: Every deployed setting is automatically deleted.
options.explanation: Assignment lifecycle is separate from deployed-resource cleanup.

options.text: They become Azure RBAC role assignments.
options.explanation: Diagnostic configuration is not converted into authorization.
Removing Policy does not produce that transformation.
